newsitem.title: CHINA: China official warns of over-optimism on trade.
newsitem.headline: China official warns of over-optimism on trade.

text.p: A senior Chinese trade official has warned against excessive optimism for good exports for the year, saying strong first quarter growth was calculated from a low base a year ago, the China Daily said on Monday.

"The first quarter's growth in exports was based upon the figures of the same period in 1996 when China's foreign trade suffered a downturn," the newspaper quote Liu Shanzai, vice-minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, as saying.
China's total trade reached $64.29 billion in the first quarter, up 11.6 percent from a year ago while exports soared 25.7 percent to $35.5 billion, creating a $6.71 billion surplus.
"It is still an arduous task to fulfil the year's $155 billion export target," Liu said.
He cited funding difficulties among state trading firms as one problem facing exports and urged domestic manufacturers to boost economic efficiency.
